America’s Quiet Exodus!

Neil deGrasse Tyson has been unusually blunt lately: he compared federal science cuts to an act of war, arguing that if a foreign rival gutted American research budgets this way, Washington would call it sabotage. Instead, it’s self-inflicted.

The numbers back him up. NSF grant awards recently hit their slowest pace in decades, with physics funding down over 80 percent and biology nearly halved. A Nature poll found roughly three-quarters of US researchers now considering leaving the country entirely.

The beneficiaries are obvious. France, Canada, and Australia are actively recruiting displaced American talent, dangling stable funding and political neutrality. China, meanwhile, has overtaken the US in total research spending, a shift analysts warn could cost America a trillion dollars in lost competitiveness over time.
Tyson’s warning isn’t nostalgia. It’s a balance-sheet argument: brains, once they leave, rarely come back.

piped.video/dYiUI6y1nKg?is=gZ0j…

Link

America’s Scientists Are Disappearing

Are we risking an America where we no longer innovate? Neil deGrass...

youtube.com ·

January: Trump’s account buys $1–5 million of Nvidia in a single trade.

April: He bans Nvidia from selling its chips to China. The stock craters, Nvidia takes a $4.5 billion write-down.

Through the spring: his accounts keep buying the dip, over a dozen Nvidia purchases.

August: He reverses his own ban. Nvidia can sell to China again, if it pays the U.S. government 15% of the revenue. A deal he cut personally.

August 18: his account buys $5–25 million of Nvidia, the single biggest stock purchase of his entire year.

December: He greenlights the even more powerful H200 chips for China, now at a 25% cut.

The President banned the stock, bought the crash, un-banned the stock, then made his biggest purchase of the year.

He controls the switch. He owns the stock. He flips the switch.

The Gemma series is an amazing set of highly performant open-weight models. They have proven extremely effective in industrial settings where site-deployed agents need exactly this as a base for domain-specific fine-tuning that even Fable-class models cannot match in accuracy.

Presumably the Gemma team has been excellent at “distilling” from the Gemini-class models to get such capabilities.

This is a $25T category. Remember, the “frontier” is not spherical. It is extremely jagged, and it isn’t just among the trillion-parameter group.

Clément Farabet (@clmt)

Very much agree with this letter.

3 years ago we started Gemma aligned with this vision, that building a thriving open weight model ecosystem was critical and likely a huge component of our future industry.

Today we continue to invest and push Gemma to be maximally useful for developers, and I’m personally very bullish on the open ecosystem it enables.

Thanks @JensenHuang and also great to see you here!
